content.title: About
content.content: Rice cooked with coconut milk is a fragrant side dish where each grain absorbs the creamy flavor of coconut. The coconut milk gives the dish a smooth, velvety texture and a subtle sweetness, making it popular in Asian and Caribbean cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut milk contains lauric acid, which gives its distinctive aroma and may support the immune system.
Traditionally, coconut rice is prepared in Thailand, Indonesia, and the Maldives.
The rice‑coconut combination has been used in ancient rituals as a symbol of abundance.
The dish is often served with mango, pineapple, or toasted peanuts for flavor contrast.
Coconut milk can be made from fresh coconut flesh or purchased in canned form.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Coconut milk provides medium‑chain triglycerides that are quickly metabolized and can serve as an immediate energy source.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Together, coconut milk and rice deliver a high amount of potassium, supporting normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in rice combined with enzymes in coconut milk promotes healthy gastrointestinal function.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Lauric acid and phenolic compounds in coconut have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune‑boosting
items.content: Lauric acid in coconut milk can be converted in the body to monolaurin, which has antiviral activity.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut milk, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Coconut milk is high in saturated fats; people with elevated cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of rice and coconut milk makes the dish calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Copper and iron balance
items.content: Large amounts of coconut milk can increase copper intake, which in excess may interfere with iron absorption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coconut rice is served as a side to curries, seafood, or grilled meats. It can also be used in desserts such as tropical puddings, or paired with fresh fruit and nuts. For extra brightness add a pinch of salt, lime zest, or grated ginger.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat by steaming or microwaving, adding a splash of coconut milk to restore its creamy texture.
